title: Unit 3 : Session 8 : SLO 2 — Restoring vs Non-Restoring Division
sections: Section C: Simulate the Algorithm (Apply): 0100 (4) ÷ 0010 (2) — non-restoring
Final correction: A = A + M = 0000. Quotient = 0010 (2), Remainder = 0000 (0) ✓
Section D: Debrief — comparing logic flow and efficiency
Efficiency: non-restoring removes the restore step, so every cycle costs exactly one addition/subtraction plus a shift — fewer operations and simpler control than restoring division.
Correction at the end: a negative final A is not a valid remainder, so the divisor is added back once to fix it.
Quotient-bit assignment: restoring sets the bit only after a possible restore; non-restoring sets it straight from the sign of A (1 if A ≥ 0, 0 if A < 0).
Logic flow: restoring = shift → subtract → if negative restore (add back) → set bit; non-restoring = shift → add or subtract depending on the sign of A → set bit → single correction at the end.
